topic_name: Jenna Ellis-Dan Scavino transfer-of-power statement evidence chain
jurisdiction: United States; Georgia criminal proceeding; federal presidential-records and congressional-records context

surface_claim.claim_text: Jenna Ellis told Fulton County prosecutors that Dan Scavino said President Trump would not leave office and that they would remain in power after the 2020 election.
surface_claim.speaker_or_institution: Jenna Ellis, attributing words to Dan Scavino
surface_claim.office_or_role: Former Trump campaign legal adviser; White House deputy chief of staff attribution
surface_claim.venue: Fulton County proffer interview; alleged White House Christmas party
surface_claim.jurisdiction: Georgia and United States federal executive context
surface_claim.source_type: news carrier with direct audiovisual discovery excerpt

claimed_justification.stated_basis: The allegation is preserved because it may bear on Scavino's understanding of Trump's post-election intent, while remaining a layered attribution rather than direct Trump speech.
claimed_justification.quoted_basis: the boss is not going to leave under any circumstances
claimed_justification.implied_basis: Scavino's proximity could make his characterization informed, but access and contextual consistency do not establish a direct instruction.

primary_records: Public audiovisual excerpt of Ellis's October 23, 2023 proffer
Official congressional report and supporting-material collection establishing Scavino access and communications role
Complete proffer, plea instruments, event records, and communications remain required
court_records: Reported Fulton County plea and protective-order proceedings; exact instruments pending acquisition
independent_analysis: Claim-level contradiction matrix and source-posture packet installed in this repository
unsupported_assertions: That Ellis personally heard Trump issue the statement
That Scavino made the statement exactly as recalled
That Scavino transmitted a direct Trump instruction
That Trump authorized a specific unlawful retention plan
That Scavino silence constitutes an admission
contradictions: No contemporaneous record or independent witness to the alleged conversation is installed
Ellis reported alcohol consumption and recalled the exchange nearly three years later
Ellis had both truthfulness and cooperation incentives and pleaded guilty to aiding false statements
The public object is excerpted rather than the complete proffer
Trump ultimately transferred office on January 20, 2021
missing_records: Complete proffer video, transcript, metadata, and discovery identifier
Plea agreement, factual basis, plea transcript, cooperation, truthfulness, breach, and statement-use terms
White House event, access, photo, video, and security records
Scavino sworn confirmation, denial, or qualification
Trump-Scavino communications tied to the alleged characterization
Original media files and social-caption provenance objects

institutional_amplifiers: House Select Committee January 6 records collection
legal_networks: Fulton County prosecutors and defense counsel
policy_documents: Presidential Records Act and applicable criminal-discovery controls remain acquisition context rather than merits findings
party_or_campaign_documents: Trump campaign and White House communications records remain required
unknown_nodes: Whether Scavino was quoting, characterizing, joking, boasting, or inferring
Whether Trump conveyed a specific instruction
Whether any operational plan was linked to the alleged words

action_conversion.instrument: No specific instrument identified in the Ellis excerpt

action_conversion.affected_population_or_program: Presidential transfer of power, election certification, public confidence, and criminal-case evidence integrity

control_comparison.comparison_notes: The immediate issue is claim attribution and corroboration, not comparative prevalence. Controls would be required for broader historical uniqueness claims.

institutional_response.judicial_status: Ellis entered a guilty plea; no adjudication establishes the Scavino conversation or Trump intent proposition.
institutional_response.administrative_status: Presidential and White House record acquisition remains pending.
institutional_response.legislative_status: Congressional records establish Scavino's proximity and nonproduction posture but not the alleged conversation.
institutional_response.oversight_status: Claim-level acquisition and independent review pending.

claimed_outcomes: Ellis alleged that Scavino expected the group to remain in power
contradicted_outcomes: The literal prediction of remaining in office under all circumstances was not the final outcome

ledger_classification.classification_notes: Proof that Ellis made the allegation is very high. Proof that Scavino said it is moderate-unconfirmed. Proof that he accurately conveyed Trump intent is moderate and contextual. Proof of a direct Trump instruction and proof of a specific unlawful plan are low from this chain alone.
